h1:
Bangsaen Beach Eats
Grab a Deckchair, Eat by the Sea
intro: The charm of Bangsaen isn't fancy restaurants — it's settling into a deckchair under an umbrella, feet in the sand right by the water, while someone brings blue crab som tam and boiled clams straight to your seat. Bangkok folks drive a little over an hour to get here, then spend the whole day in the cool sea breeze with plates of spicy food. This is your guide to what to order, where to sit, roughly what it costs, and what to know before you go.
chips: 🦀 Blue crab som tam & boiled clams
🚗 An easy food trip near Bangkok

blocks.html: Bangsaen is the beach that locals from Chonburi and Bangkok know best, because it's close and easy to eat at. The heart of it is the deckchairs and canvas umbrellas lined up the whole length of the sand — rent a chair and you can sit all day. Before long a vendor walks past with blue crab som tam, boiled clams, grilled squid, boiled corn, even ice cream, and you can order right from your chair without getting up. If you want a proper sit-down meal, just walk up to the restaurants on the beach road. This article focuses on the real Bangsaen beachside eating experience — if you're after a full sit-down seafood restaurant, see the Chonburi seafood guide linked at the end.

blocks.text: How the deckchairs work and what they cost

blocks.html: Once you've parked and walked down to the sand, vendors who own the deckchairs will wave you over to their stall — you pick where you want to sit. Rental is charged per spot, and a deckchair generally runs around 30–40 THB for the whole day with no time limit. Some vendors set up a table of 4 seats for around 120–150 THB. The stall owner usually takes your seafood orders too, cooks it fresh right there, and brings it to your chair.

items: Deckchair fee — around 30–40 THB per chair, all day; a table of 4 runs about 120–150 THB
Order straight from your chair — the stall owner takes orders for boiled/grilled seafood, som tam, fried rice and snacks
Agree on the price first — ask up front what the chair and the dishes cost so there are no surprises at the bill
Roaming vendors — grilled squid, boiled corn, fried meatballs, ice cream and fruit pass by constantly if you want to add more

blocks.title: No deckchairs on the beach on Tuesdays
blocks.html: The municipality sets Tuesday as beach cleaning day, with no deckchairs and no vending allowed along the sand. If your plan is to sit in a deckchair and eat by the sea, skip Tuesday and pick another day. Saturdays and Sundays are the busiest, so come a bit early to grab a good spot right by the water.

blocks.text: Bangsaen beachside dishes you have to order

blocks.html: Bangsaen food leans bold and punchy, the kind you eat with a sea breeze — boiled seafood with spicy seafood dipping sauce, fiery som tam, and fragrant grilled bites are the stars. Order a spread to share between a few people and it works out cheaper while you get to try more.

items.name: Blue crab som tam (tam pu ma)
items.blurb: Papaya salad with fresh sweet blue crab, spicy and savory — Bangsaen's signature plate that almost every stall makes. Eat it with sticky rice and the sea breeze.

items.name: Boiled clams / cockles
items.blurb: Cockles or surf clams boiled just until done, dipped in spicy seafood sauce with garlic. Freshness shows here, and it's easy to order and easy to keep eating.

items.name: Grilled squid
items.blurb: Skewered squid grilled fragrant off a cart that rolls past your chair, dipped in seafood sauce — the beach snack you can't skip.

items.name: Fried oyster omelette (hoy tod)
items.blurb: Oysters in a crispy-edged, soft-centered batter, scattered with bean sprouts and eaten with chili sauce. Known spots like Khun Nit Hoy Tod start around 35–45 THB.

items.name: Grilled prawns
items.blurb: Big sea prawns grilled in the shell, springy and sweet, dipped in seafood sauce. Order it as a special plate when there are several of you — priced by size.

items.name: Boiled quail eggs with dipping sauce
items.blurb: A cheap nibble — boiled quail eggs dipped in Maggi sauce with chili, dirt-cheap and the perfect thing to pick at while you wait for the mains.

blocks.text: Top spots around Hat Won & Bangsaen Soi 2

blocks.html: If you've had your fill of sea breeze and want a serious meal, the Hat Won Napha area and Bangsaen Soi 2 have yam (spicy salad) and spicy-food spots where locals meet up in the evening. We've picked only places that have real reviews from people who actually ate there and that are open now.

items.name: Pa Mon Hat Won Super Kai Kai
items.blurb: A famous yam spot in the Hat Won area that's run for years — from a pushcart into a sit-down shop. Bold flavors, generous portions, and locals call it Bangsaen's go-to for spicy food. Regular orders are blue crab som tam with fresh prawns, blue crab yam, yam moo yor with salted egg yolk and pla ra, and the stewed-soft chicken-leg super soup.

items.name: Prim Yam Pu Ma Bangsaen (Indy Market)
items.blurb: A blue crab yam shop in Bangsaen's Indy Market, focused on fresh firm crab tossed in a spicy dressing at friendly prices. Good for a bite before hitting the beach, or to take back and eat at your deckchair.
items.meta: Indy Market Bangsaen · fresh blue crab yam · about ฿100–250/person

items.name: Pa Chup Yam Saep Bangsaen (Lot 37)
items.blurb: A beachside yam shop people seek out for its loaded crab-roe and crab-meat yam, fully seasoned and punchy. Stock turns over fast — a Hat Won-style yam spot that reviewers mention often.
items.meta: Hat Won, Lot 37 · crab roe & crab meat yam · about ฿100–250/person

items.name: Khun Nit Hoy Tod
items.blurb: A long-running fried oyster omelette spot in Bangsaen — crisp batter, packed with oysters, starting around 35–45 THB. An easy, cheap beach snack, good for a quick bite while you sit in your deckchair.
items.meta: Bangsaen area · old-school hoy tod · from ฿35–45/plate

items.name: Andy's Seafood Bangsaen
items.blurb: A made-to-order seafood shop in the Bangsaen area, cooked fresh — stir-fried squid, fried fish, and stir-fried seafood plates. Single dishes start cheap, good for anyone who wants seafood at a table without trekking onto the sand.
items.meta: Bangsaen area · made-to-order seafood · plates from ฿35+

items.name: Tu Seafood Bangsaen
items.blurb: A dinner seafood spot in the Bangsaen area focused on grilled and stir-fried plates — grilled prawns, grilled shellfish, and stir-fried squid. Honest home-style cooking that Bangsaen locals bring people to for a relaxed dinner.

items.name: Phetchaburi Curry-and-Rice by Bangsaen Beach
items.blurb: A cheap curry-and-rice shop by the beach — pick from several dishes starting around 30 THB, with free veggies and chili dip. Good for a budget lunch before or after a swim.
items.meta: By Bangsaen Beach · cheap curry-and-rice · from ฿30/plate

items.name: Grilled Fresh Seafood by Pa Aed
items.blurb: A grilled seafood and som tam shop in the Bangsaen area — fresh seafood grilled fragrant, eaten with spicy som tam. Bold flavors that suit people who like it hot, at the friendly prices of a beachside shop.
items.meta: Bangsaen area · grilled seafood + som tam · about ฿150–300/person

blocks.title: Order smart and avoid anything not fresh
blocks.html: For seafood like blue crab, prawns and clams ordered from a deckchair stall, ask the price per plate or per kilo before you agree, and check whether the stock is turning over fast. Yam, som tam and fried rice dishes usually have fixed prices and work out better value when there are several of you. For grilled snacks off a cart, pick a vendor grilling fresh in front of you and don't eat anything that's been sitting around.

faq.q: How much does it cost to rent a deckchair on Bangsaen Beach?
faq.a: A regular deckchair runs around 30–40 THB each, all day with no time limit. Some vendors set up a table of 4 seats for around 120–150 THB. The stall owner usually takes your seafood orders too. Ask the price of the chair and the dishes up front before you sit down.

faq.q: What food is there on Bangsaen Beach?
faq.a: The stars are blue crab som tam, boiled clams, boiled cockles, grilled squid, fried oyster omelette and grilled prawns — all orderable right from your deckchair. There are also roaming vendors selling boiled corn, fried meatballs, fruit and ice cream. Most prices are affordable, and ordering to share between a few people works out cheaper while you get to try more.

faq.q: Why are there no deckchairs on Bangsaen Beach on Tuesdays?
faq.a: The municipality designates Tuesday as beach cleaning day, with no deckchairs and no vending along the sand. If your plan is to sit in a deckchair and eat by the sea, skip Tuesday and pick another day instead.

faq.q: Which spicy yam shop by Bangsaen Beach do people recommend?
faq.a: Pa Mon Hat Won Super Kai Kai on Bangsaen Soi 2 is the yam shop locals talk about most. It's open evening to late and is known for blue crab som tam with fresh prawns, blue crab yam, and the chicken-leg super soup. There's also Prim Yam Pu Ma in the Indy Market, and Pa Chup, known for its crab roe and crab meat yam.

faq.q: When is the best time to eat by Bangsaen Beach?
faq.a: Late afternoon into evening is most comfortable — the sea breeze is cool and you get the soft evening light on the sand. Saturdays and Sundays are busiest, so if you want a good deckchair right by the water, come from morning to mid-morning. Weekdays are quieter and it's easier to pick a seat — just remember to avoid Tuesday, when there are no deckchairs.
